key_concept: Mango's taxonomic hierarchy (Genus Mangifera, Family Anacardiaceae, Order Sapindales, Class Dicotyledonae, Division/Phylum Angiospermae) and the standard plant suffixes that identify each rank.
steps: A. Family: in plants the suffix '-aceae' marks a family, so Anacardiaceae is the family of mango. A–III.
B. Genus: Mangifera is the genus in the binomial *Mangifera indica*. B–V.
C. Class: mango is a dicot, so its class is Dicotyledonae. C–II.
D. Phylum/Division: mango is a flowering plant, so its division is Angiospermae. D–IV.
E. Order: the suffix '-ales' marks an order in plants, so Sapindales is mango's order. E–I.
Combining the pairs gives A–III, B–V, C–II, D–IV, E–I, which is exactly option (4).
final_answer: Option (4): A-III, B-V, C-II, D-IV, E-I
why_not_others: Option (1) swaps family and order (Sapindales is an order, Anacardiaceae a family). Options (2) and (3) wrongly assign Dicotyledonae to family and Mangifera to class or Sapindales to genus, ignoring the rank suffixes.
common_trap: Students confuse family and order, forgetting that '-aceae' denotes a family and '-ales' denotes an order.
time_saving_tip: Use the suffixes first: '-aceae' gives Family = Anacardiaceae (A–III), which leaves only option (4). '-ales' giving Order = Sapindales (E–I) confirms it instantly.
